title: Stag hunt — repeated encounters
description: Repeated stag hunt for MeltingPot-comparable measurement. The stag respawns at the same location 5 turns after each cooperative capture; hares respawn 8 turns after pickup. The match runs the full turn budget regardless of captures — what matters is your cumulative score across many encounters. Each encounter is the same dilemma: commit to the stag (high cooperative payoff, requires partner) or pick up hares (low solo payoff, no coordination needed). With repeated play, agents can build (or break) trust over time.
goal: Maximize cumulative reward across 100 turns. Stag captures (cooperative, both adjacent same turn) yield 5 split among captors; hare pickups yield 1 each. Both stag and hares respawn after a cooldown. Trust-building across repeated encounters is the strategic axis: defection on one stag attempt may damage cooperation on later encounters.
notes: Phase C/D MeltingPot 2.0 lineage extension (2026-05-01). Compares to MeltingPot's stag_hunt_in_the_matrix__arena (25×24 grid, 8 players, ~5000 frames). We use 24×24 + 2 players + 100 turns — agent count and episode length are smaller for LLM-cost reasons; mechanism is comparable.
Repeated mode key difference from single-shot stag_hunt_01: match never terminates on stag capture; cumulative scoring across all encounters; respawn cooldowns; per-agent score breakdown in result.
Cooperation-stable equilibrium: both pursue stag every encounter → ~10 captures × 2.5 each = 25 reward each (over 100 turns at 10-turn cycle = stag respawn 5 + travel ~5).
Defection equilibrium: both pursue hares only → ~6-8 hare pickups each (4 hares × ~10 respawn cycles).

Mixed: one cooperates, one defects → cooperator gets 0 stag (no partner) + hares = ~6-8; defector gets 0 stag + many hares since solo. Worst for defector if cooperator commits to stag and abandons hares.
